prompts.question: How do you determine the terms in the quotient when dividing two polynomials?

prompts.question: How can you use the Factor Theorem and synthetic substitution to quickly determine any factors of (P(x))?
prompts.answer: If (P(a)=0), then (x-a) is a factor. The bottom line of synthetic substitution gives the coefficients of the other factor. The first term of that factor is one degree less than the first term of (P(x)).

prompts.question: How do the Remainder Theorem and Factor Theorem compare?
prompts.answer: The Remainder Theorem states that when (P(x)) is divided by (x-a), the remainder is equivalent to (P(a)). The Factor Theorem states that the binomial ((x-a)) is a factor of (P(x)) if and only if (P(a)=0). The Factor Theorem is a special case of the Remainder Theorem, describing the situation when the remainder is zero.
